summary: This article explains how many bats find their way and catch insects in the dark by listening to echoes, why they are not blind, and how they help farms and wild plants, including in Saudi Arabia.
introduce: Read the title “Bats Use Echoes to See” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: finding things by sending out sounds and listening to the echoes that come back
an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal
how high or low a sound is

challengeTerms.def: describing sound that is too high for human ears to hear
to find your way from one place to another
how many times a sound wave vibrates each second; it decides whether a sound is high or low

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that bats are more helpful to people than most people think? Use evidence from the article to explain.
The article says people copied the bats' trick to build sonar.
struggling: Pre-teach echolocation, prey, and pitch with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use ultrasonic, navigate, and frequency in a short paragraph that states the main idea of the article in their own words.
